title: seed: on a walled boot the organization-create replay runs before the founder's sys_member row is written, so the new organization's own seed cannot resolve any person, the founder included
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUg7BKfRBcTPyMxbLh

Filing gate ③: area-directed (area S2 of seat domain:server#5; out-of-scope item of #33791, named in review-b PASS 6898091549 on PR #34023, item 7). Follow-up of #33791.

## Today

On a walled (`isolated`) boot, `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/create` replays the app's seed into the new organization before the founder's `sys_member` row is written. In #33791's reproduction log, the replay is at 10:36:52.150Z and the `sys_member` insert at 10:36:52.175Z. Seed person references (`Field.user()`, `Field.lookup('sys_user')`, and the injected `owner_id` once PR #34023 lands) resolve membership-scoped on an organization's load. That replay therefore cannot resolve anyone: every such column gets NULL plus "not a member of organization ORG", and that includes the founder, who is the one person certain to be a member. Only a later install into the organization, or a reseed, reaches existing members.

## Ask

Measure first, in the runtime organization-create path (`packages/runtime`, the hook that replays seeds on organization create, and the auth plugin's member write):
1. Confirm the order on main, with the walled showcase boot from #33791.
2. If the order is as logged, decide between running the replay after the founder's `sys_member` row commits, or leaving it and saying so. Leaving it could be acceptable, because the first-admin handoff claims NULL `owner_id` rows; it does not fill declared `Field.user()` columns, though.

## Prior rulings read

#33791 (body, "Related observation, not this card"); PR #34023 review PASS 6898091549, item 7 (left unfiled for the area to dispose). No ⛔ line on replay ordering found in ADR-0105 (tenancy posture). The first-admin handoff in runtime `app-plugin.ts` claims NULL owners only.

## Reader

domain:server, area S2 (A4, seed and runtime boot). Size S–M (measure first).
